conviction_note: The evidence points both ways and nearly cancels. Peers show weaker grocery volume (Kroger's identical sales ex-IRA slowed about 70bp in an overlapping quarter, and Circana's August perishables units fell sharply) and Walmart is taking share. Against that, Kroger held its profit guide despite cutting sales, the Q2 consensus (EPS $0.31-0.33, EBITDA ~$770M, -9% y/y) sits below the pace the FY guide implies for the rest of the year, insiders bought about $2.5M after the July cut, and short interest rose 23% to 59.5M shares (~12% of shares outstanding, 7.5 days to cover). Findings sum to +0.9. The scaled number is p_up 52 x abs 7.5 = +0.3. It is smaller than the sum because the put skew (+9.4 vol pts) and the interim-CFO / new-executive-chair reset risk argue for staying near 50.
bar: Q2 FY26 (12 weeks to 2026-09-12). EPS consensus: $0.31 at Earnings Whispers (whisper $0.34, revenue $18.83B; https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/ACI) and ~$0.33 at Investing.com 2026-10-12 (revenue $18.9B, EPS estimates 'edged up modestly over 60 days'; https://investing.com/news/earnings/albertsons-earnings-up-next-can-aci-edge-turn-around-grocery-93CH-4944664). Adjusted EBITDA consensus ~$770M; RBC is at $761M with identical sales -1% (https://finimize.com/content/rbc-thinks-albertsons-q2-could-miss-by-a-hair, undated page). Company FY26 guide from 2026-07-23: identical sales -1.5% to -0.5% (incl. ~150bp IRA headwind), adjusted EBITDA $3.55-3.625B, adjusted EPS $1.75-1.85 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000041/aciq126earningsrelease.htm). The two EPS sources roughly agree. The EBITDA bar rests on one source. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on adjusted EBITDA.
positioning_check: Short interest (FINRA via equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/aci/shortinterest, read 2026-10-12): 59,495,647 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 7.48 days to cover. That is up from 48.3M on 2026-07-31 (+23%) and 55.96M on 2026-09-15, so shorts have built steadily since the guide cut. Against 485.3M Class A shares outstanding on 2026-07-24 (10-Q cover) that is ~12.3% of shares outstanding, and a higher share of float if insiders and sponsors hold a block. That counts as crowded for a large-cap grocer. Options (baseline): 25-delta skew +9.38 vol pts (downside paid), event-implied move 6.65%, put/call OI 0.44 (call OI heavier), ATM spread 18% of mid. Tape: 5-day run-up +6.99%, 20-day -3.18%, 37.6% below the 52-week high. Insider buys after the July cut: EVP Moriarty $1.96M at $11.51 (07-27), CEO Morris $450k at $11.42 (07-28), CFO McCollam $103k (07-31).

findings.finding: Kroger, whose Q2 (May 24-Aug 15, 2026) overlaps most of ACI's Q2 (Jun 21-Sep 12), saw identical sales ex-fuel slow from +1.0% in Q1 to +0.2% in Q2 (IRA drag 130bp then 138bp, so ex-IRA ~2.3% to ~1.6%). It cut its FY identical-sales guide to 0.2-0.8% from 1.0-2.0%, citing 'the macro environment'. Circana data (Grocery Dive, 2026-09-17) show August unit sales of produce -6.7%, bakery -4.3% and meat -2.3% y/y. Applying Kroger's ~60bp two-year-stack slowdown to ACI's Q1 (-0.8% on a +2.8% compare; Q2 compare is +2.2%) gives Q2 identical sales of roughly -0.8% to -1.2%. That is near RBC's -1% and inside ACI's own FY guide of -1.5% to -0.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-23, Q1 identical sales of -0.8% with a guide cut gave -21.64%. On 2025-10-14, Q2 identical sales of +2.2% with a beat and raise gave +13.63%. Identical sales and the guide move this stock together.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: RBC's -1% and the -1.5% to -0.5% guide already assume a negative comp. What is new is the direction of change: a direct peer slowed in the overlapping weeks, after ACI last spoke on 07-23. If the market had fully priced a weaker-than-Q1 comp, EPS estimates would have drifted down. Instead they 'edged up modestly over 60 days' (Investing.com 2026-10-12), and the stock is +7% over 5 days.
findings.independence: Circana August unit data via Grocery Dive, a different source: https://www.grocerydive.com/news/august-tough-month-grocery-unit-sales-perishables/830644/ (2026-09-17). Kroger Q1 baseline: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000056873/000110465926075395/tm2618219d1_ex99-1.htm. This is a peer proxy, not an ACI number.

findings.finding: Walmart U.S. (Q2 FY27, reported 2026-08-20) posted mid-single-digit grocery comps 'driven by unit volume gains and share gains' and is putting ~$2.9B of tariff refunds into price rollbacks. ACI's CEO named Walmart, Amazon and Aldi as the main share-takers on the July call. RBC says further downside would come from more ACI 'price investment', which would squeeze the margin the guide depends on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 cut (-21.6%) was blamed on consumer pressure and share loss to price-led competitors, with investment accelerated 'ahead of expected productivity benefits'. Margin and guide news moves this stock in double digits.
findings.why_not_priced: The share-loss story has been public since July, and the put skew already pays for downside. The new element is a competitor funding rollbacks with a one-off refund during ACI's Q2 and Q3. If that were priced, the Q2 EBITDA bar would sit at or below RBC's $761M rather than $770M, and EPS estimates would not be rising.
findings.independence: ACI CEO on July competition: https://www.webull.com/news/15282425096463360. RBC price-investment risk: https://finimize.com/content/rbc-thinks-albertsons-q2-could-miss-by-a-hair. This is a proxy plus inference. ACI has not confirmed new price investment since 07-23.

findings.finding: Kroger kept its FY26 profit guide (adjusted FIFO operating profit $5.0-5.2B, EPS $5.10-5.30) despite cutting sales. Its FIFO gross margin ex-fuel rose 13bp, helped by 'favorable pharmacy mix' and 'strong pharmacy' performance. ACI's Q1 10-Q says pharmacy margins improved 'mainly because of the IRA's impact'. So the same IRA drag that hurts comps (Walmart 125bp, Kroger 138bp, ACI guided ~150bp) supports gross margin, which makes holding the $3.55-3.625B EBITDA guide more plausible than the sales trend alone suggests.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2025-10-14, a guide raise gave +13.63%. On 2026-07-23, a guide cut gave -21.64%. A reaffirmation after a cut has no clean precedent in the seven prints. Kroger's own reaction on 2026-09-11 could not be sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades at ~6.7x the midpoint of its own EPS guide and sits 11.7% above its 52-week low. With 59.5M shares short and the put skew paying for downside, the market is pricing a second cut more than a hold. If a hold were the base case, short interest would not have risen 23% since July and the skew would be flatter. RBC expects the guide to be held.
findings.independence: Shares one document with the first finding (Kroger 8-K), read for a different line (profit vs sales). ACI's own pharmacy-margin language: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000046/aci-20260620.htm. Walmart IRA 125bp: https://www.grocerydive.com/news/walmart-second-quarter-fiscal-2027-earnings-grocery/828292/.

findings.finding: The Q2 bar is set below the pace the FY guide implies. FY guide adjusted EBITDA is $3.55-3.625B less Q1's $1,013M, which leaves $2.54-2.61B for the remaining 36 weeks. FY25 delivered $3,901.5M less Q1's $1,111M less ~$68M for the 53rd week, about $2.72B, so the guide implies -4% to -7% y/y for the rest of the year. Q2 consensus EBITDA of ~$770M is ~-9% and EPS of $0.31-0.33 is -25% to -30% vs $0.44, both worse than that pace and in line with or worse than Q1 (-8.8% EBITDA, -24% EPS). An in-line or slightly better Q2 with a reaffirmed guide would show the guide holding, while a Q2 at consensus forces a back-half acceleration that the market will question.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 EPS of $0.42 missed consensus of $0.54 (-22%) together with a guide cut: -21.64%. Q2 FY25 EPS of $0.44 beat ~$0.39-0.40: +13.63%.
findings.why_not_priced: Arithmetic from two company releases, against estimates sourced at Earnings Whispers and Investing.com. If the market read Q2 as the trough, sell-side previews would frame a beat as likely. RBC instead previews a small miss ($761M vs $770M), and Earnings Whispers' whisper of $0.34 is the only sign of a lean the other way.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 figures and the guide: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000041/aciq126earningsrelease.htm. Consensus: https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/ACI. This is my inference across these documents.

findings.finding: Three insiders bought in the open market after the July cut, about $2.5M in total: EVP M&A/Corporate Affairs Thomas Moriarty 170,500 shares at $11.51 ($1.96M, 2026-07-27), CEO Susan Morris 39,409 shares at $11.42 ($450k, 2026-07-28) and CFO Sharon McCollam 9,000 shares at $11.48 ($103k, 2026-07-31). Spot is $12.315.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the Form 4s are 2.5 months old. What it adds is that management bought into the guide they had just set, one week after setting it. That is evidence against a second cut being planned at that time, though not proof.

findings.finding: Leadership has been overhauled since the last print. Meg Whitman was named to the new role of Executive Chair on 2026-09-08 ($8.9M RSU grant, also advising the CEO on strategy). Three new directors join effective 2026-10-14, taking the board from 11 to 14. CFO McCollam stepped down and SVP Treasury/IR Cody Perdue became interim CFO on 2026-09-30, so this is his first call. The retail-media head left and media was folded into merchandising (Grocery Dive, 2026-10-09). A new executive chair and an interim CFO raise the odds of a reset on the call (a new strategy framing, ACI Edge cost targets, or a rebased guide), and the sign of that reset is genuinely uncertain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CFO retirement and restructuring were announced alongside the 07-23 guide cut (-21.64%). There is no clean precedent for a print under new leadership.
findings.why_not_priced: Each event was public, but none has been read through to the guide. No preview found ties Whitman's arrival to a guide or capital-allocation reset. If it were priced, the event-implied move (6.65%) would sit nearer the last print's 21.6% than the 5.96% median.
findings.independence: Whitman 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000054/aci-20260908.htm. Media reorganisation: https://www.grocerydive.com/news/albertsons-media-collective-consolidating-departments-merchandising-media-operations/832605/. All are company-sourced facts, and the direction is my inference.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 48.3M shares (2026-07-31) to 59.5M (2026-09-30), 7.48 days to cover, ~12.3% of the 485.3M shares outstanding. The 5-day run-up is +7.0%, so some covering or positioning has started. A print that merely reaffirms the guide into this short base gives a squeeze its own mechanism, as the +13.6% on the October 2025 beat-and-raise showed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-14 beat and raise: +13.63%. Upside moves on this name are large when the guide surprises up. Short interest at that time is unknown.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew still pays for downside (+9.4 vol pts), so options are positioned for a miss, not a squeeze. If the squeeze risk were priced, the skew would be flatter and call implied vol bid.
findings.independence: Share count from the 10-Q cover: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000046/aci-20260620.htm. Run-up from the sealed baseline.

outside_window.finding: ACI's Delaware Chancery suit against Kroger, seeking the $600M merger termination fee (about $1.24 per share, ~10% of market cap) plus damages, goes to trial on 2026-10-19 per the Q1 10-Q, with Kroger counterclaiming. The trial date is after the window. A pre-trial settlement disclosed on the 10-13 call would land inside it, but nothing points to one.

The Washington State opioid bench trial against Albertsons/Safeway began 2026-07-13, and the statute-of-limitations defense was struck on 2026-07-29. It is excluded from the $773.8M settlement framework. No verdict date has been found, so it is not expected inside the window.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The negatives (peer volume slowdown, Walmart share gains) agree with the +9.4 put skew and are therefore largely priced. The positives (low Q2 bar against the guide, Kroger holding profit, insider buying, a crowded and growing short) cut against the skew and fit the +7% 5-day run-up. That leaves p_up only slightly above 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): Kroger/Circana comp finding moved from -1.0 to -0.6, because a -1% Q2 identical-sales figure sits inside ACI's -1.5% to -0.5% FY guide and RBC already has it.

Rule 5 (proxy) and rule 7 (crowded short vs negative): Walmart competitive-pressure finding moved from -0.8 to -0.6. It is an unconfirmed transmission into a 12%-short name, and the put skew already pays for it.
Rule 5 (proxy): Kroger profit-hold finding moved from +0.8 to +0.6, since it is a peer read-through, not an ACI number.
Rule 3 (own caveat): leadership-overhaul finding moved from -0.5 to -0.3, because its own text says the sign of a reset is genuinely uncertain. The wide band was kept.
Rule 1 (fact is not reaction): insider-buying finding moved from +0.4 to +0.3, since the Form 4s are 2.5 months old and public.
Left unchanged: low-bar arithmetic +0.5 (two agreeing EPS sources, so rule 6 does not cap it) and the short-interest positioning +1.0. abs_move 7.5 and p_up 52 were left as drafted.
